messages.author: b419b3f42893b2f1
messages.subject: Upload image files in Shiny
parts:
Hi all,

I'm struggling to find a way to use fileInput() to read image files (.tiff) using the function readImage() from the EBImage package.

I don't understand the details of how fileInput() works, but I get the error:
Unable to determine type of C:\...\Temp\Rtmpcj8dOj/08de162c4d17e93f78cadb23/0: Filename extension missing.

when I do 

readImage(files = input$inFile$datapath)

I assume that the above is a path to where the file is temporary stored, but now doesn't have a file extension which the function I read with needs.

Is there a general way to get around this? I've had similar problems with an "specialized file reading function" before, but gave up trying...

Is there a smooth way to get the filepath to "original" file on my local computer?

Many thanks,
Anders

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: Re: Upload image files in Shiny
parts:
To answer your last question: I don't think you need the original path from your local computer, it sounds like perhaps the function you're using just needs the file to have its original filename (including extension).  When you upload a file using fileInput, the names of the file after being uploaded are NOT the same as the name of the file on your computer, so I sometimes use this bit of code to rename the uploaded files to match their real filenames.  Maybe this is all you need.

#' When files get uploaded, their new filenames are gibberish.
#' This function renames all uploaded files to their original names
#' @param x The dataframe returned from a shiny::fileInput
fixUploadedFilesNames <- function(x) {
 if (is.null(x)) {
   return()
 }
 
 oldNames = x$datapath
 newNames = file.path(dirname(x$datapath),
                      x$name)
 file.rename(from = oldNames, to = newNames)
 x$datapath <- newNames
 x
}
